security_hardening.title: Sanitize high score display to prevent stored XSS
security_hardening.description: The updateHighScoresDisplay() function in highscores.js (lines 686-688) uses innerHTML with user-provided initials and scores loaded from localStorage. While the in-game UI restricts input to alphanumeric characters via the CHARACTERS constant, an attacker could directly manipulate localStorage to inject malicious HTML/JavaScript payloads.
security_hardening.rationale: Stored XSS via innerHTML allows attackers to inject persistent malicious scripts. An attacker with localStorage access (browser DevTools, other XSS, malicious extension) could set initials to '' which would execute whenever high scores are displayed.
security_hardening.vulnerability: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)
security_hardening.currentRisk: Attacker with localStorage access can inject persistent XSS. While game-only context limits impact, could be used for phishing overlays or credential harvesting if users treat the game page as trusted.
security_hardening.remediation: Replace innerHTML with safe DOM APIs. For highscores.js line 686-688, use createElement/textContent: const div = document.createElement('div'); div.className = 'score-entry'; div.textContent = `${index + 1}. ${entry.initials} - ${entry.score}`. Alternatively, validate stored initials match /^[A-Z0-9]{1,3}$/ before rendering.

security_hardening.title: Add localStorage data validation to prevent prototype pollution
security_hardening.description: The loadHighScores() function uses JSON.parse() on localStorage data without schema validation. While wrapped in try-catch, malformed JSON with __proto__ or constructor properties could cause prototype pollution. The glow intensity in main.js also parses localStorage values without bounds checking.
security_hardening.rationale: Prototype pollution can lead to unexpected behavior or security bypasses. Validating the structure of parsed data ensures it conforms to expected schema before being used in the application.
security_hardening.vulnerability: CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes
security_hardening.currentRisk: Malformed localStorage data could pollute object prototypes. Glow intensity values are not validated to be within the expected 0-3 range.
security_hardening.remediation: Add schema validation after JSON.parse: validate each entry has {initials: string (3 chars A-Z0-9), score: positive integer, date: positive integer}. Use Object.hasOwn() checks. For glow intensity, validate parseFloat result is finite and within [0,3] range. Consider using a simple schema validator function.

security_hardening.title: Implement Content Security Policy for defense-in-depth
security_hardening.description: The application has no Content Security Policy (CSP) configured in index.html or via headers. CSP is a critical defense-in-depth mechanism that restricts which scripts, styles, and resources can be loaded and executed.
security_hardening.rationale: CSP limits the impact of XSS vulnerabilities by whitelisting only trusted script sources. Even if XSS is possible, CSP can prevent execution of injected scripts. This is particularly important since the application uses inline styles extensively.
security_hardening.currentRisk: No defense-in-depth protection against script injection attacks. Any XSS vulnerability can execute arbitrary scripts without restriction.
security_hardening.remediation: Add CSP meta tag to index.html head section: <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self';">. For CDN development mode, add https://cdn.jsdelivr.net and https://unpkg.com to script-src. For production hosting, configure CSP header at the web server level.

security_hardening.title: Add security headers configuration for production deployment
security_hardening.description: The application lacks standard security headers that protect against common web vulnerabilities. When deployed to a static hosting platform, headers like X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy should be configured.
security_hardening.rationale: Security headers provide defense-in-depth. X-Frame-Options prevents clickjacking (embedding game in malicious iframe), X-Content-Type-Options prevents MIME sniffing, and Permissions-Policy restricts browser feature access.
security_hardening.currentRisk: Game could be embedded in malicious iframes for clickjacking. No restriction on browser feature access requests.
security_hardening.remediation: Create a headers configuration for your deployment platform. For Netlify, create _headers file: /* X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(), microphone=(), camera=(). For Vercel, use vercel.json headers config. For GitHub Pages, these headers are not configurable but CSP meta tag provides partial mitigation.

security_hardening.title: Establish dependency update and audit cadence
security_hardening.description: The project uses THREE.js v0.158.0 (released October 2023) and Vite v5.4.x. While no critical CVEs are currently known, the dependencies are over a year old. The vite-plugin-obfuscator package has limited maintenance activity and may introduce supply chain risk.
security_hardening.rationale: Dependencies can have security vulnerabilities discovered after release. THREE.js is now at v0.170+ and may include security or stability fixes. Regular updates reduce technical debt and attack surface.
security_hardening.vulnerability: CWE-1104: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
security_hardening.currentRisk: Older dependencies may contain unpatched vulnerabilities. The vite-plugin-obfuscator package adds complexity with questionable security benefit - code obfuscation is not a security control.
security_hardening.remediation: 1. Run 'npm audit' periodically to check for known CVEs. 2. Consider updating THREE.js to latest stable (test 3D rendering thoroughly for breaking changes). 3. Set up Dependabot or Renovate for automated PR creation. 4. Evaluate whether vite-plugin-obfuscator is needed - obfuscation provides minimal protection and the package may have supply chain concerns.

metadata.analysisNotes: This is a client-side browser game with a limited attack surface. No backend, authentication, or sensitive data processing beyond local high scores. Primary concerns are XSS via localStorage manipulation and missing defense-in-depth headers. The .auto-claude directory (containing any env files) is properly gitignored.
